infused once the conditioning regimen is complete, usually 
after several days, and the day of stem cell infusion is referred 
to as day 0.
Th e conditioning regimen serves two purposes: (1) to provide 
suﬃ  cient immunosuppression to prevent rejection and allow 
engraftment of donor stem cells, and (2) to eradicate malignant 
cells. Major toxicities are associated with the conditioning regi-
men (high-dose chemotherapy and/or total body radiation). 
Patients may also experience toxicities that occur as a result of 
graft rejection, known as graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), and
infectious complications associated with immunosuppression. 
GVHD only occurs in those individuals receiving an allogeneic
